instructions: Rinse the rice in a sieve until the water runs mostly clear. Put it in a pot with 2 1/4 cups water and a pinch of salt. Bring it to a boil, then turn the heat to low, cover, and cook for 15 minutes. Leave it covered, off the heat, until the cauliflower is done.

Cut the cauliflower into medium florets. Soak them in 3 cups of warm water, not hot, for 5 minutes. Drain, rinse under cold water, then dry them very well on a clean towel. Wet florets make a soggy coating.

In a large bowl, whisk the flour, the cornstarch, 1/2 tsp of the black pepper and 1/2 tsp of the salt. Add 1 cup water a little at a time, whisking, until the batter is smooth and thick enough to coat a spoon.

Mince the garlic and ginger. Slice the green onions, keeping the white parts and the green parts in separate piles. Finely chop the bell pepper. In a small bowl, stir together 2 tbsp soy sauce, 3 tbsp ketchup, 1 tbsp rice vinegar, 2 tsp sugar, the paprika and 1/3 cup water.
Pour 2 1/2 cups of the oil into a wide heavy pan, about 3/4 inch deep, and heat it over medium heat. Test it with a drop of batter. It should sizzle and rise without browning.

Toss half the florets in the batter and lower them into the oil one by one. Leave them alone for 2 minutes so the coating sets. Then turn the heat to medium-low and fry for 4 to 5 minutes more, turning now and then, until golden and crisp. Transfer them to a tray lined with paper towels. Fry the second half the same way.

Pour the oil out of the pan into a heatproof bowl and let it cool. Wipe the pan. Heat the remaining 3 tbsp oil over high heat. Add the garlic, ginger and the white parts of the green onion. Stir for 1 minute.

Add the bell pepper and cook for 2 minutes, until it starts to soften. Pour in the sauce mixture and cook for 2 minutes, until it thickens. Stir in the remaining 1 tsp black pepper and take the pan off the heat.
Let the sauce cool for 1 minute, then add the fried cauliflower and toss to coat. Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Scatter the green parts of the green onion over the top. Serve right away over the rice, with the sriracha at the table for anyone who wants heat.
method_notes: Lead is Swasthi's Recipes (5.0 from 571, as shown on the page): florets in a flour and cornstarch batter, fried until crisp, then tossed in a garlic, ginger, soy, ketchup and vinegar sauce. Other cooks double-fry or bake or air fry for less oil, and a few add egg to the batter, which is left out so it stays vegan. The lead's chili sauce is moved to the table as sriracha and ketchup carries the sauce, and the Kashmiri chili for color becomes paprika, which the lead allows. Amounts are doubled from the lead, and it is fried in a wide pan about 3/4 inch deep rather than deep fried.
